findings.issue: Heart Rate Measurement Sensor Contact flags are inverted vs Bluetooth SIG HRS v1.0: Support is bit 2 (0x04), Status/detected is bit 1 (0x02). parse sets supported=(flags&0x02) and detected=(flags&0x04); encode always ORs 0x02 for “support” and 0x04 for contact. Real Polar/SIG payloads will report supported/detected backwards; encode→parse only “works” because both sides share the same wrong mapping.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse: sensorContactSupported = (flags & 0x04) !== 0; sensorContactDetected = supported && (flags & 0x02) !== 0. Encode: flags |= 0x04 for support; if contact detected flags |= 0x02. Add fixture tests for flags 0x00 (unsupported), 0x04 (supported no contact), 0x06 (supported+contact) per HRS 3.1.1.1.2.
findings.evidence: heartRate.ts L115-116, L178-179; HRS v1.0: “Sensor Contact Support bit (bit 2)”; “Sensor Contact Status bit (bit 1)” for skin contact when supported.

findings.issue: Browser/Hermes bytesToBase64 builds Base64 via repeated string += fromCharCode, O(n²) for large payloads (scan records, long reads). base64ToBytes also does not validate padding/alphabet: Node Buffer.from(...,'base64') silently accepts garbage; atob throws uncaught DOMException—inconsistent and unsafe for untrusted peripheral data decoded in-app.
findings.proposed_fix: Chunk encode (e.g. 0x8000) or use btoa on joined chunks; optionally prefer globalThis.Buffer when present. Reject invalid Base64 with TypeError (strict alphabet/padding) on both paths; add Encoding.test invalid vectors.
findings.evidence: encoding.ts:54-57 binary += String.fromCharCode; 29-30 Buf.from(base64,'base64') without validation; __tests__/Encoding.test.js only happy-path vectors

findings.issue: FakeBlePort.emitNotification shares one Uint8Array copy across all monitor listeners; a mutating listener corrupts others. PortBleManager.monitorCharacteristicForDeviceAsBytes then copies again, but Base64 path and multi-subscriber Fake tests can still observe shared mutation. BluezBlePort correctly does per-listener new Uint8Array(value).
findings.proposed_fix: Match Bluez: for (const cb of listeners) cb(new Uint8Array(value)). Add fanout mutation isolation test.
findings.evidence: BlePort.ts:320-323 single copy then for-loop cb(copy); BluezBlePort.ts:395 per-cb new Uint8Array(value)

findings.issue: FakeBlePort stores service tree keys with the original UUID string case, while value map keys use charKey (lowercased). discoverCharacteristics/services are case-sensitive; read/write via charKey are case-insensitive. Seed with mixed-case SIG UUIDs and query with canonical lowercase can return empty discovery while R/W still works—or the reverse depending on ensureChar path—breaking port contract assumptions used by shared apps.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalize service and characteristic UUID keys with expandBluetoothUuid/normalizeUuidKey (same as discovery/uuidMatch) in tree and charKey. Contract test: seed uppercase UUID, discover/read with lowercase.
findings.evidence: charKey 92–94 lowercases; ensureChar/tree 165–168 uses raw serviceUUID; discoverCharacteristics 234–238 looks up exact serviceUUID key.

findings.issue: startDeviceScan on web both invokes the listener with OperationNotSupported and throws the same error. ROADMAP listener/subscription rule says report typed error once through the listener channel and start no native work; dual channel surprises awaiters and apps that only handle one path. Tests only assert throw, not listener invocation or errorCode.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one shipped contract: prefer listener-once + resolved void (or rejected promise without double-notify), document it, and test both errorCode and single delivery. Keep PortBleManager plain Error path from diverging if web host is the public surface.
findings.evidence: web.ts:314-320 listener(err,null); throw err; ROADMAP.4.0 capability contract: 'Listener/subscription operations… reports the same typed BleError… exactly once'.
